To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SARA and ERBIN are interacting partners, and that the ERBID domain of ERBIN is a novel SARA-interacting domain.
SARA and ERBIN compete for binding to SMAD2 and 3 and that SARA can reverse the inhibitory effect on SMAD2 and/or SMAD3-dependent transcription of ERBIN.
SARA and ERBIN are new partners that interact with each other and with SMAD2 or SMAD3, and that SARA and SMADA/SMAD3 compete for binding to ERBID.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of proteins that are involved in TGF-β signalling.
the identification and characterization of new SARA-interaction partners, which will provide new insights into the regulation of TGFβ signalling.
the molecular mechanisms that control cell growth and differentiation in response to extracellular signals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ERBIN, SARA and SMADS are all involved in the regulation of TGFβ signaling, and that the relative concentrations of these proteins determine the final outcome of TGFβ/activin signaling in a cell.
ERBIN, a new SARA binding partner, competes with SARA for binding to SMAD2 and -3 and inhibits SMAD2 and 3-mediated transcription.
ERBIN is an endosomal adaptor protein which interacts with SARA and SMADS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ERBIN is an important regulator of SMAD2/SMAD3 signalling and its role is to inhibit SMAD2/Smad3 signalling.
ERBIN can be considered a new SARA-binding protein that competes with SMADS for binding to ERBID.
ERBIN is an important regulator of TGFβ signalling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SARA, ERBN and SMADs compete for binding to ERBN and that this competition can influence the response of cells.
SARA, ERBID and SMAD2 compete for binding to ERBID.
ERBIN is an important new player in the TGFβ signalling pathway.
